c-m3-solids.label: Cone, prism and sphere: the formulas that matter
c-m3-solids.summary: A handful of formulas cover the exam: cone slant height, prism volume, sphere and cylinder volumes.

c-m3-displace.label: Immersed solid: volume in = volume of water raised
c-m3-displace.summary: A solid dropped into a vessel raises the water by exactly its own volume.

q-m3-cone.label: Slant height, radius or height of a cone
q-m3-cone.summary: Two of radius, height and slant height are known; find the third (Pythagoras).

q-m3-prism.label: Prism or cuboid volume after a change
q-m3-prism.summary: Base area and height give the volume; a height change scales it.

q-m3-displace.label: Sphere dropped into a cylinder of water
q-m3-displace.summary: Sphere volume equals cylinder volume of the water rise; solve for the radius.

formulas.text: Cone: l² = r² + h²     V = ⅓πr²h     curved area = πrl
Prism / cylinder: V = base area × height     Cylinder: V = πr²h
formulas.note: Height up 25% means volume × 1.25 with the same base.

q-m3-cone.cue: 'A right circular cone has radius … and height …. Slant height?'
q-m3-cone.fast: Recognise the triple 9–40–41; no squaring needed.
q-m3-cone.eliminate: The slant height is just over the height (40) because the radius is small: l is between 40 and 49. Only 41 is just above 40.
traps: Giving the height of 40 as the slant height.
Using the volume formula with a ⅓ instead of Pythagoras.

q-m3-prism.cue: A base area and a height, and the height changes by a percentage.
q-m3-prism.eliminate: Volume must rise by exactly 25% from 432, so it is above 432 and below 600. Strike 432 (no change).
traps: Using the ⅓ factor of a pyramid.

q-m3-displace.cue: 'A solid sphere is completely immersed in a cylindrical vessel…water level rises by…'.
q-m3-displace.fast: Volume of the sphere ÷ rise = πR²: 288 ÷ 4 = 72 gives R² = 72 = 36 × 2.
q-m3-displace.eliminate: R² = 72 lies between 64 and 81, so R lies between 8 and 9. Check the options: 6√2 ≈ 8.49 fits; 4√2 ≈ 5.7 and 5√2 ≈ 7.1 are too small, and 8√2 ≈ 11.3 is too large.
traps: Using the sphere's radius as the cylinder's radius.
Leaving R² = 72 without taking the root.
